# Best rechargeable AA batteries

For most people, I'd pick the Panasonic Eneloop Pro for high-drain gear, or IKEA LADDA if you want the cheapest good option.

## Picks

**Best overall (cameras, flashes, controllers): Panasonic Eneloop Pro**
- Digital Camera World names it best overall, and its reviewer has used it for years to test speedlights. GearLab also picks it for high-drain devices.
- GearLab lists the 4-pack (BK-3HCCA4BA) at $17.99 and says it holds about 85% charge after a year in a drawer.
- Panasonic rates Pro for fewer recharge cycles than standard Eneloop, so you trade some cycle life for capacity.
- I don't have a direct store link for it. The Digital Camera World guide links to Adorama, Amazon, Newegg and Best Buy: https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA**
- Charge-Test says these are very likely Eneloop-based, and its measurements held up well even at a 1A load.
- IKEA's US page lists the 1900 mAh AA 4-pack at $9.99, or $8.99 with the STENKOL charger: https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/
- GearLab's $7.99 price for the higher-capacity 2450 mAh version is for in-store purchase. I couldn't confirm that model or price on IKEA's US site, so check your local store.

**Best in bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO 2,800 mAh, 20-pack ($42.99)**
- It's rated for 1,200 cycles and 85% charge remaining after a year.
- [Buy the 20-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack)
- If you need a charger, the [Tenergy TN480U 8-bay ($23.99)](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger) works with it. The box has no power adapter.
- These are affiliate links, and the source says it's paid if you buy. That source also only had Tenergy in its records, so it never compared Tenergy with Eneloop or LADDA.

## Caveats
- **Capacity claims:** Treat "2800 mAh" ratings with caution. Frame & Focal's testing says Amazon Basics' 2800 mAh cells delivered about 2,247 mAh at a low load and much less at 2A. That site's two articles also don't fully agree with each other, so I'd weigh them less than the other sources.
- **Voltage:** NiMH cells are 1.2V, so a few devices built for 1.5V alkalines may show a low-battery reading. Digital Camera World mentions newer 1.5V lithium-ion AAs as an alternative, but I don't have prices for them.
- **Charger:** You need an NiMH charger. IKEA's STENKOL bundle or the Tenergy charger above would work.

If you tell me what you'll use them in (remotes, a camera, toys, a flashlight), I can narrow it down.
